_notes.announce.tier: A fragment with a LEADING SPACE, spliced mid-sentence into the sub messages. Keep the leading space and keep the word Tier in English.
_notes.announce.tierParen: A fragment with a LEADING SPACE, appended after the verb. Keep the leading space.
_notes.announce.sub.streak: A fragment with a LEADING COMMA AND SPACE, appended mid-sentence before the tier fragment. {months} is always 2 or more. Write the word for 'month' out IN FULL and inflect it for the number if the language requires it; English uses the attributive singular ('a 12 month streak'), which most languages do not.
_notes.announce.saidMessage: Has a LEADING SPACE and is appended to a preceding sentence. {subject} is a pronoun fetched per viewer (he/she/they/neopronoun). Use {g} to inflect the verb: it is he, she, or other.
_notes.announce.redemption.input: {text} is the already-built announcement; this only joins it to the viewer's message.
_notes.announce.yt.superchat: Ends with a colon and a TRAILING SPACE; the viewer's message is appended after it.
_notes.announce.yt.superchat.amount: Ends with a colon and a TRAILING SPACE; the viewer's message is appended after it.
_notes.announce.pronoun.subject: The subject pronoun used when a viewer's pronouns are unknown. English uses the singular they.
_notes.emoji.wrap: Wraps one emoji read aloud, e.g. '(fire emoji)'. {description} is a noun phrase. No count: it is always exactly one.
_notes.emote.wrap: Wraps one chat emote read aloud, e.g. '(dancing cat emote)'. No count: it is always exactly one.
_notes.emote.fallback: Read instead of a description when describing the emote failed. Just the emote's own name, with nothing around it.
_notes.emote.fallback.repeated: The same, for an emote repeated more than once: the count and the name, bracketed.
_notes.emoji.wrap.repeated: The same for an emoji repeated, e.g. '(3 fire emojis)'.
_notes.emote.wrap.repeated: The same for an emote repeated, e.g. '(3 dancing cat emotes)'.
_notes.cmd.setting.user.current: {property} is a noun phrase like 'speed preference'. {usage} is the command's syntax line and must be copied through untouched — it contains the literal chat command.
_notes.cmd.setting.channel.current: As above. {usage} is command syntax; do not translate what it contains.
_notes.cmd.setting.invalid: {hint} is a separate sentence, already translated.
_notes.cmd.defaultlanguage.current: {docLink} is a URL; copy it exactly.
_notes.cmd.hint.languages: {docLink} is a URL; copy it exactly.
_notes.cmd.hint.emotions: {list} is a comma-separated list of emotion names that are NOT translated — they are the literal values a viewer types.
_notes.cmd.value.channelDefault: Shown in place of a value when the viewer has set no preference of their own.
_notes.cmd.property.languageBoost: The provider's term for the synthesis language hint.
_notes.cmd.mode.current: The quoted '!tts mode <all|command|bits|points>' is the literal command a viewer types. Copy it exactly, including the option words.
_notes.cmd.mode.invalid: 'all', 'command', 'bits' and 'points' are the literal values a viewer types. Copy them exactly.
_notes.cmd.queue.paused: PAUSED is capitalised for emphasis in chat; keep whatever emphasis is natural.
_notes.cmd.profanity.effect.on: A clause, not a sentence: it is spliced into several replies after a dash. No leading capital, no full stop.
_notes.cmd.profanity.state.on: ON is the filter's state, shown in capitals for emphasis. {effect} is the clause above.
_notes.cmd.profanity.note.auto: Has a LEADING SPACE; it is appended to the sentence before it. "auto" is a literal setting value — keep it.
_notes.cmd.profanity.coverage.low: Has a LEADING SPACE; appended mid-sentence.
_notes.cmd.profanity.usage: {usage} is the command's syntax line; copy it through untouched. "on" and "off" are the literal words a moderator types.
_notes.cmd.profanity.already: {setting} is the literal word on or off. {effect} is the clause above.
_notes.cmd.profanity.status: {coverage} and {note} are optional clauses that already carry their own leading space.
_notes.cmd.profanity.turnedOn: {note} is an optional clause that carries its own leading space.
_notes.cmd.onOff.on: A state word spliced into other messages, shown in capitals for emphasis in chat.
_notes.cmd.events.current: The quoted '!tts events <on|off>' is the literal command; copy it exactly.
_notes.cmd.events.invalid: 'on' and 'off' are the literal words a moderator types.
_notes.cmd.permission.current: Everything after 'Usage:' is the literal command and its option words; copy it exactly.
_notes.cmd.permission.invalid: 'everyone', 'all', 'subs', 'vip' and 'mods' are literal values a moderator types.
_notes.cmd.ignore.listPrefix: Ends with a TRAILING SPACE; a comma-separated list of names follows it.
_notes.cmd.ignore.listMore: Ends with a TRAILING SPACE. Used on the second and later messages when the list is too long for one.
_notes.cmd.bits.current: 'Bits' is Twitch's currency. Everything after 'Use ' is the literal command; copy it exactly.
_notes.cmd.bits.needAmount: The example command in brackets is literal; copy it exactly.
_notes.cmd.status: {engine} and {paused} are already-translated words. {channel} is a channel name — never translate it.
_notes.cmd.voice.current: The quoted commands are literal; copy them exactly. {value} is a voice ID and is never translated.
_notes.cmd.voice.currentUnset: The quoted command is literal; copy it exactly.
_notes.cmd.defaultvoice.invalid: {docLink} is a URL. '!tts voices' is a literal command. {value} is a voice ID.
_notes.cmd.ignore.usage: Every quoted '!tts ...' is a literal command; copy them exactly. {user} is the viewer's own login name.
_notes.cmd.ignore.addDenied: The quoted command is literal. {user} is the viewer's own login name.
_notes.cmd.ignore.added: {user} is a display name or login; never translate it.
_notes.cmd.pronounce.usage: {usage} is the command's syntax line; copy it through untouched.
_notes.cmd.pronounce.noneCustom: Everything after 'Add one with: ' is a literal command; copy it exactly.
_notes.cmd.pronounce.entry: A list row: the word, an arrow, and how it is spoken. Both values are channel data, never translated.
_notes.cmd.pronounce.entryOff: A list row for a built-in the channel switched off.
_notes.cmd.pronounce.listMore: Has a LEADING SPACE; appended to the list before it.
_notes.cmd.pronounce.notBuiltIn: The quoted '!tts pronounce remove ...' is a literal command; copy it exactly.
_notes.cmd.pronounce.switchedOff: Everything after 'Restore it with: ' is a literal command; copy it exactly.
_notes.cmd.pronounce.badSay: {reason} is a sentence fragment such as 'cannot be empty', already translated separately.
_notes.cmd.emote.usage: Every '!tts emote ...' form is a literal command; copy them exactly.
_notes.cmd.emote.needName: The usage part is a literal command; copy it exactly.
_notes.cmd.emote.notChannel: {channel} is a channel name and {name} an emote name; never translate either.
_notes.cmd.emote.view: {descriptions} is a comma-separated list of quoted descriptions, already in this language.
_notes.cmd.noPermission: {subcommand} is the literal subcommand name the viewer typed; never translate it.
_notes.cmd.failed: {command} is the literal command name; never translate it.
_notes.player.stale: 'Refresh' is the exact wording of OBS's own right-click menu item. Use OBS's translation of that menu item if the software is localized, otherwise leave it in English.
